intent.raw_query: New Zealand South Island, $4000, hiking and bungee jumping, November 2026

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Take the ultimate leap from New Zealand's highest bungy jump at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. This iconic AJ Hackett experience includes a scenic gondola ride to the pod suspended above the canyon and delivers an adrenaline rush unlike any other in the Southern Hemisphere.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Great Walk
experiences.description: Hike one of New Zealand's nine Great Walks through stunning alpine scenery connecting Fiordland and Mount Aspiring National Parks. The trail winds past glacial lakes, ancient beech forests, and dramatic mountain passes offering breathtaking panoramic views of the Southern Alps.

experiences.name: Franz Josef Glacier Valley Walk
experiences.description: Explore the terminal face of the famous Franz Josef Glacier on a guided valley floor walk through rainforest and glacial moraine. Witness towering ice formations and learn about the glacier's dynamic movement in one of the world's rare places where a glacier descends into a temperate rainforest.

experiences.name: Milford Sound Kayaking and Hike Combo
experiences.description: Paddle through the majestic fiords of Milford Sound surrounded by sheer 1200-meter cliff faces and cascading waterfalls, then hike a section of the Milford Track through ancient rainforest. Spot seals, dolphins, and rare Fiordland penguins in one of the world's most dramatic natural landscapes.

experiences.name: Queenstown Night Food and Culture Walk
experiences.description: Explore Queenstown's vibrant culinary scene on a guided evening walk sampling local Central Otago pinot noir, South Island lamb dishes, fresh blue cod, and artisan cheeses at iconic local eateries. Discover the town's gold rush history and Māori cultural heritage through storytelling at key landmarks along the lakefront.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - New Zealand South Island
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Queenstown Airport at 13:00. Collect luggage and take the Orbus public bus (Route 1, ~NZD 2) into Queenstown town centre. Check in to Nevis Valley, Queenstown Boutique Stay. Take a short walk along the Queenstown Bay waterfront to get your bearings, enjoy views of Lake Wakatipu and The Remarkables mountain range.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Queenstown town centre and explore the lively pedestrian mall. Visit the Queenstown Gardens (free entry) for a relaxing evening walk along the lake shore.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at Queenstown Airport
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and affordable bite at Fergburger (iconic Queenstown burger joint, ~NZD 14-16) after settling in
meals.dinner: Self-cater from a nearby Pak'nSave or Countdown supermarket to save money on your first night (~NZD 8-12 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Pick up an Orbus card or use contactless payment for cheap local bus travel. Stock up on groceries for breakfasts and snacks throughout the trip to keep costs down. The Nevis Valley area is approximately 45 minutes from Queenstown centre.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early and hike the Queenstown Hill Time Walk (Te Tapu-nui). This free 2-3 hour return hike starts from Belfast Terrace and rewards you with panoramic 360-degree views of Lake Wakatipu, Queenstown, and the surrounding mountain ranges. Elevation gain ~490m.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Kawarau Gorge Suspension Bridge — the world's first commercial bungee jump site operated by AJ Hackett (~NZD 150-165 for the 43m jump). Even if you skip the jump, watching others leap is free and thrilling. Explore the nearby Kawarau River gorge walking tracks.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown and explore the waterfront. Watch the sunset over Lake Wakatipu from the Queenstown Bay boardwalk (free). Browse the night markets if it's a Thursday (Queenstown Night Market).

meals.breakfast: Self-catered oats or toast at accommodation (~NZD 2-3)
meals.lunch: Pack a homemade sandwich and snacks for the hike
meals.dinner: Vudu Cafe & Larder or The Cow Restaurant for affordable pizza and pasta (~NZD 18-22)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Kawarau Bungee in advance online for potential discounts. Wear sturdy hiking shoes for the Queenstown Hill walk. The Kawarau Bridge is about 23km from Queenstown — take a shuttle or rideshare (~NZD 10-15 each way).

day_by_day.morning: Drive or take a shuttle to Glenorchy (~45 minutes from Queenstown, free scenic drive). Walk the Glenorchy Lagoon Walkway (1.5 hours, free) through wetlands with stunning mountain reflections. This area was used as a filming location for Lord of the Rings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue on the Glenorchy-Paradise Road to the Paradise area (gravel road, 4WD recommended or walk the last section). Explore the beech forest and open meadows. Alternatively, hike part of the Rob Roy Glacier Track starting point near Glenorchy (~2 hours partial return, free).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown. Relax and recover from the day's activities. Visit the Queenstown waterfront for the golden hour light on The Remarkables.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation
meals.lunch: Pack lunch from home — eat with views at the Glenorchy lakefront picnic area
meals.dinner: Wok This Way or a local takeaway in Queenstown (~NZD 12-16)

day_by_day.notes: The Glenorchy drive is one of the most scenic in New Zealand and is completely free. Check road conditions on the Glenorchy-Paradise Road before heading out. Consider carpooling with other hostel guests to split fuel costs.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Intercity or Naked Bus to Wanaka (~1 hour, ~NZD 15-25). Drop bags at a locker or your next stop. Walk the Roys Peak Track (8 hours return, 1,578m elevation) — start early to reach the summit for iconic views over Lake Wanaka. This is one of New Zealand's most photographed hikes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Roys Peak summit hike or, if you started very early, begin the descent and enjoy the views on the way down. The trail rewards with sweeping views of Mt Aspiring National Park.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Wanaka town. Explore the lakefront, visit the famous 'That Wanaka Tree' (a lone willow growing from the lake, free photo opportunity). Enjoy the relaxed Wanaka vibe.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast before the hike (energy-rich oats or muesli)
meals.lunch: Pack substantial trail snacks and lunch — essential for the long Roys Peak hike
meals.dinner: Kai Whakapai Cafe & Bar or Francesca's Italian Kitchen for a well-deserved affordable meal (~NZD 18-24)

day_by_day.notes: Roys Peak is a strenuous full-day hike — start no later than 7:00am. Carry at least 2 litres of water per person, sunscreen, and layers. The track can be busy in November; weekday mornings are quieter. Book return bus to Queenstown in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Wanaka town and the free Wanaka lakefront. Walk the easy Lake Wanaka Outlet Track (1.5 hours return, free) along the lake edge through willow and beech forest to the outlet where Lake Wanaka meets the Clutha River.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Puzzling World (~NZD 16-22) — a quirky attraction with optical illusions and a famous tilted building, great value for a couple of hours. Alternatively, hike the Diamond Lake and Rocky Mountain Track (2-3 hours, free) for outstanding views over Lake Wanaka.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown via Intercity bus or rideshare (~NZD 15-25). Settle back at Nevis Valley accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Grab a cheap breakfast from New World supermarket in Wanaka (~NZD 4-6)
meals.lunch: Picnic by the lake with supermarket supplies
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at accommodation or Fergburger in Queenstown (~NZD 14-16)

day_by_day.notes: Wanaka is a wonderful alternative base to Queenstown with a more relaxed atmosphere. The Diamond Lake track is highly recommended as a free alternative to paid activities. Check bus timetables in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Experience the Nevis Bungy by AJ Hackett — New Zealand's highest bungee jump at 134m, located in the dramatic Nevis Valley right near your accommodation (~NZD 275). Book the first slot of the day. The gondola ride to the pod suspended above the Nevis River is an experience in itself.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the adrenaline rush, recover with a scenic walk in the Nevis Valley area. Explore the rugged schist rock landscapes and tussock-covered hills surrounding the valley. The Nevis Bluff area offers incredible high-country scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown base. Celebrate your bungee achievement with a budget-friendly dinner and a drink at a local pub.

meals.breakfast: Light self-catered breakfast before the jump
meals.lunch: Pack snacks — there are limited food options in the Nevis Valley
meals.dinner: The Sherwood or World Bar for affordable drinks and food (~NZD 15-20). Happy hour deals available at many Queenstown bars.

day_by_day.notes: The Nevis Bungy is the flagship experience given your accommodation location. Book well in advance as slots fill quickly, especially in November (peak season). Transport to the Nevis Valley jump site is included in the ticket price from Queenstown. Weight and health restrictions apply.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day after the Nevis Bungy. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely morning at the accommodation. Take a gentle walk around the Nevis Valley surroundings to appreciate the high-country landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head into Queenstown. Walk the Tiki Trail — a free 45-minute hike up to the Skyline Gondola top station (save the ~NZD 32 gondola fee). Enjoy the panoramic views of Queenstown and Lake Wakatipu from the top for free.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Queenstown's lively Saturday night atmosphere. Visit the Queenstown Night Market (Thursdays) or browse local shops. Enjoy the vibrant lakefront.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered big breakfast at accommodation to recover
meals.lunch: Grab a cheap lunch at the Queenstown Countdown deli or a food truck
meals.dinner: Fishbone Bar & Grill for affordable fish and chips or try Bao Now for budget Asian bao buns (~NZD 12-18)

day_by_day.notes: Your body will appreciate a lighter activity day after the Nevis Bungy. The Tiki Trail is a great way to access the Skyline views without paying the gondola fee — it's steep but manageable in about 45 minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early bus or drive to Te Anau (~2.5 hours from Queenstown, Intercity ~NZD 25-35). Check in to a budget hostel (YHA Te Anau or similar, ~NZD 30-40/night). Walk the Te Anau Lake Trail along the lakefront (free, 1-2 hours).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Te Anau town and the Department of Conservation (DOC) visitor centre (free) to learn about Fiordland National Park. Walk the Control Gates area and enjoy views of Lake Te Anau — the South Island's largest lake.
day_by_day.evening: Relax in Te Anau and prepare for the next day's Milford Sound adventure. The town is small and peaceful — enjoy the alpine atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered before departure from Queenstown
meals.lunch: Pack lunch for the bus journey or buy from a Te Anau cafe on arrival (~NZD 10-14)
meals.dinner: Miles Better Pies or The Fat Duck Te Anau for affordable local food (~NZD 15-20)

day_by_day.notes: Te Anau is the gateway to Fiordland and Milford Sound. Book your Milford Sound day trip/cruise in advance. Consider the Milford Sound day cruise (~NZD 55-75 for budget operators like RealNZ or Go Orange). Intercity bus from Queenstown to Te Anau is the most budget-friendly option.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Te Anau at 7:00am for Milford Sound via the stunning Milford Road (SH94). Stop at the Mirror Lakes (free), Avenue of the Disappearing Mountain (free), and the Homer Tunnel. Arrive at Milford Sound (~2 hours drive).
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a budget Milford Sound nature cruise (1.5-2 hours, ~NZD 55-75 with Go Orange or similar budget operator). See Mitre Peak, Stirling Falls, Bowen Falls, and watch for dolphins, seals, and penguins. The cruise includes stunning views of sheer cliff faces plunging into the fiord.
day_by_day.evening: Return drive to Te Anau along the Milford Road. Stop at the Chasm Walk (free, 30 minutes return) to see the powerful Cleddau River carving through sculpted rock. Arrive back in Te Anau by evening.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Pack lunch to eat at Milford Sound — food at the terminal is expensive
meals.dinner: Self-catered at Te Anau hostel or Sandfly Cafe (~NZD 12-18)

day_by_day.notes: The Milford Road is one of the world's most scenic drives — allow extra time for photo stops. Book the Milford Sound cruise well in advance as November is busy. Go Orange and Jucy Cruise offer the most budget-friendly options. Check weather forecasts — Milford Sound receives 7-8m of rain annually but is beautiful in any weather.

day_by_day.morning: Hike the Kepler Track Day Walk — take the water taxi across Lake Te Anau (~NZD 25 return) to the Brod Bay campsite and hike through stunning beech forest to the Luxmore Hut (approximately 4-5 hours one way, or turn around at Brod Bay for a shorter 2-hour option). Views of Lake Te Anau and Fiordland are spectacular.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Kepler Track hike or return via the water taxi. The track above the bush line offers incredible alpine views if you push to the higher sections.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Te Anau town. Pack up and prepare for travel the next day. Enjoy a final Te Anau dinner.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast
meals.lunch: Pack a substantial trail lunch and snacks for the Kepler hike
meals.dinner: Fiordland Brewing Company for craft beer and affordable pub meals (~NZD 18-24)

day_by_day.notes: The Kepler Track is one of New Zealand's Great Walks but you don't need to book the full multi-day walk to enjoy day sections. The water taxi makes the day walk much more rewarding. Wear waterproof layers — Fiordland weather can change rapidly.

day_by_day.morning: Return bus from Te Anau to Queenstown (~2.5 hours, Intercity ~NZD 25-35). Arrive back at Nevis Valley accommodation. Freshen up and rest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Queenstown Bike Park or explore the Queenstown Trail (free walking/cycling trail network). Walk or hire a cheap bike (~NZD 15-20/hour) along the Frankton Arm lakefront trail — a beautiful flat 5km path with mountain views.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy your last full evening in Queenstown. Walk along the waterfront and take in the views of The Remarkables at sunset. Browse the shops on the pedestrian mall.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered before departure from Te Anau
meals.lunch: Pack lunch for the bus journey
meals.dinner: Treat yourself slightly — Rata Restaurant has a more affordable lunch menu, or try Bespoke Kitchen for healthy affordable bowls (~NZD 18-22)

day_by_day.notes: The Queenstown Trail is a free and excellent way to explore the area on foot or by bike. November daylight hours are long (sunset ~9:00pm) so there's plenty of time for an evening activity.

day_by_day.morning: Final big hike day — tackle the Ben Lomond Track (5-6 hours return, free). This is the most rewarding hike near Queenstown, reaching 1,748m elevation with 360-degree views over Lake Wakatipu, The Remarkables, and beyond. Start from the Skyline car park via the Tiki Trail.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend Ben Lomond and return to Queenstown. Soak tired feet at the lakefront. Visit any last-minute attractions or do some souvenir shopping at budget-friendly options (Queenstown Night Market on Thursdays for unique local gifts).
day_by_day.evening: Thursday Night Market in Queenstown — browse local food stalls, crafts, and street performers. Great budget dining option with diverse food stalls (~NZD 8-15 for a full meal). Celebrate the end of an incredible trip!

meals.breakfast: Hearty self-catered breakfast before the Ben Lomond hike
meals.lunch: Pack substantial trail food and plenty of water
meals.dinner: Queenstown Night Market — try multiple stalls for a varied and affordable feast (~NZD 12-18 total)

day_by_day.notes: Ben Lomond is the crown jewel of Queenstown hiking — do not miss it if the weather is clear. Check the forecast the night before and have a backup plan. The track above the Skyline is exposed and can be cold/windy even in November. Start by 8:00am for the best conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in New Zealand. Enjoy a slow breakfast and pack up. Take a last walk along the Queenstown Bay lakefront to soak in the views of Lake Wakatipu and The Remarkables. Visit the Queenstown Gardens one final time (free).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Nevis Valley accommodation. Head to Queenstown Airport via Orbus public bus (~NZD 2) or arrange a shuttle (~NZD 15-20). Allow 2 hours before departure for check-in and security. Depart Queenstown.
day_by_day.evening: Departure or in transit. Reflect on an incredible 13 days of hiking, bungee jumping, and South Island adventures.

meals.breakfast: Final self-catered breakfast or treat yourself to a cafe breakfast in Queenstown (~NZD 12-18 at Vudu Cafe or Bespoke Kitchen)
meals.lunch: Grab airport food or pack remaining supplies for the journey
meals.dinner: In transit or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Allow plenty of time to get to the airport — Queenstown Airport can get busy with departures. Use up any remaining New Zealand cash at the airport or donate to charity bins. Keep a small budget buffer for airport meals and transport. Total estimated budget for 13 days excluding flights: NZD 1,400-1,900 per person (accommodation ~NZD 400-500, activities ~NZD 600-700 including both bungees, transport ~NZD 200-250, food ~NZD 300-400).

trip_options.title: Classic New Zealand South Island Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Take the ultimate leap from New Zealand's highest bungy jump at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. This iconic AJ Hackett experience includes a scenic gondola ride to the pod suspended above the canyon and delivers an adrenaline rush unlike any other in the Southern Hemisphere.

The trail winds past glacial lakes, ancient beech forests, and dramatic mountain passes offering breathtaking panoramic views of the Southern Alps.

Witness towering ice formations and learn about the glacier's dynamic movement in one of the world's rare places where a glacier descends into a temperate rainforest.

experiences.description: Paddle through the majestic fiords of Milford Sound surrounded by sheer 1200-meter cliff faces and cascading waterfalls, then hike a section of the Milford Track through ancient rainforest. experiences.name: Queenstown Night Food and Culture Walk
experiences.description: Explore Queenstown's vibrant culinary scene on a guided evening walk sampling local Central Otago pinot noir, South Island lamb dishes, fresh blue cod, and artisan cheeses at iconic local eateries. Discover the town's gold rush history and Māori cultural heritage through storytelling at key landmarks along the lakefront.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Queenstown Airport at 13:00 - no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer from Queenstown Airport to Nevis Valley, Queenstown Boutique Stay. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll around the Queenstown lakefront to get your bearings and enjoy views of The Remarkables mountain range
day_by_day.evening: Join the Queenstown Night Food and Culture Walk - explore Queenstown's vibrant culinary scene on a guided evening walk sampling local Central Otago pinot noir, artisan cheeses, and regional delicacies while learning about the town's gold rush history

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at Queenstown Airport - try Vudu Cafe for a fresh sandwich and flat white coffee
meals.dinner: Included tastings on the Night Food and Culture Walk; supplement with a sit-down meal at Rata Restaurant for modern New Zealand cuisine using locally sourced ingredients (mid-range, ~NZD 45-65 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the 13:00 arrival. Allow time for jet lag recovery. Confirm boutique stay check-in time in advance. The Night Food Walk typically departs around 6:00 PM - book in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Prepare for the ultimate adrenaline experience - take the Nevis Bungy shuttle from central Queenstown to the Nevis River gorge. Complete the Nevis Bungy Jump, New Zealand's highest bungy at 134 meters. The freefall lasts approximately 8.5 seconds. Arrive early for briefing and harnessing
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Queenstown and recover with a scenic walk along the Queenstown Hill Time Walk (2-3 hours return), offering panoramic views over Lake Wakatipu and the surrounding mountains - a perfect gentle contrast to the morning adrenaline
day_by_day.evening: Relax and celebrate your bungy jump achievement. Browse the Queenstown waterfront and enjoy the sunset over Lake Wakatipu

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the boutique stay or nearby - try a hearty meal before the jump. Vudu Larder on Rees Street for eggs and avocado toast (~NZD 20-25)
meals.lunch: Fergburger - Queenstown's legendary burger institution, iconic mid-range option (~NZD 15-20). Expect a queue but worth it
meals.dinner: The Cow Restaurant - cozy stone building serving pizza and pasta, excellent value for money, beloved local institution (~NZD 30-40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Nevis Bungy must be booked in advance through AJ Hackett. Minimum weight 45kg, maximum 127kg. Wear comfortable, secure clothing. Video and photo packages available for purchase on the day. The shuttle departs from the AJ Hackett Station in central Queenstown.

day_by_day.morning: Drive or take a scenic bus from Queenstown toward Te Anau (approximately 2 hours). Stop at Kingston and the scenic Lake Wakatipu shoreline en route. Check in to Te Anau accommodation and prepare gear for the Routeburn Track
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Te Anau Glowworm Caves on a guided boat tour across Lake Te Anau - an extraordinary underground limestone cave system filled with thousands of tiny glowworms creating a natural starscape (approximately 2 hours)
day_by_day.evening: Explore Te Anau township, a charming gateway town to Fiordland. Walk along the lakefront at dusk when the mountains reflect beautifully on the still water

meals.breakfast: At the boutique stay in Queenstown before departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or stop at Mossburn on the drive - The Mossburn Country Park Cafe for pies and coffee
meals.dinner: Redcliff Restaurant in Te Anau - rustic cottage atmosphere serving venison, lamb and fresh fish with Fiordland-inspired menu (~NZD 40-55 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book Te Anau Glowworm Caves in advance through Real Journeys. Depart Queenstown early enough to arrive in Te Anau by early afternoon. The drive via State Highway 6 and 94 is scenic and worth taking slowly. Arrange Te Anau accommodation separately for nights 3-4.

day_by_day.morning: Drive the stunning Milford Road (SH94) from Te Anau to Milford Sound (approximately 2 hours). Stop at Mirror Lakes, The Chasm, and Homer Tunnel along the way for photos and short walks
day_by_day.afternoon: Experience the Milford Sound Kayaking and Hike Combo - paddle through the majestic fiords surrounded by sheer 1200-meter cliff faces, spotting seals, dolphins and waterfalls. The combo includes a guided hike on the valley floor through ancient rainforest
day_by_day.evening: Return drive to Te Anau along Milford Road, watching the golden evening light paint the mountain peaks. Arrive back in Te Anau by early evening

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast in Te Anau before the drive - Sandfly Cafe for eggs and strong coffee (~NZD 18-22)
meals.lunch: Pack your own lunch for the kayaking and hike combo, or purchase from the Milford Sound Lodge cafe on arrival
meals.dinner: The Fat Duck in Te Anau - popular local bistro with generous portions of New Zealand lamb, salmon and vegetarian options (~NZD 35-50 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Depart Te Anau by 7:30 AM to allow time for roadside stops and arrive for your kayak session. Book the Milford Sound Kayaking and Hike Combo well in advance - this is a popular activity. Check weather conditions as Milford receives very high rainfall. Bring waterproof gear and insect repellent for sandflies.

day_by_day.morning: Begin Day 1 of the Routeburn Track Great Walk. Shuttle from Te Anau to The Divide trailhead (or Routeburn Shelter). Hike from The Divide to Lake Howden Hut (approximately 3-4 hours, 8km) through beech forest and past Key Summit alpine gardens
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue hiking from Lake Howden toward Routeburn Falls Hut (approximately 4-5 hours, 11km), passing through stunning alpine meadows, the Hollyford Valley lookout, and cascading waterfalls
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Routeburn Falls Hut (1000m elevation), settle in, meet fellow trampers, and enjoy the extraordinary mountain panorama as the sun sets over the Harris Mountains

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Te Anau accommodation before shuttle departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the trail - prepare the night before with sandwiches, trail mix, muesli bars and fruit
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at the hut using the cooking facilities - pack dehydrated meals or pre-prepared pasta. Huts have gas cookers and basic utensils

day_by_day.notes: The Routeburn Track requires a Great Walk booking through DOC (Department of Conservation) made well in advance - these sell out months ahead. Pack all essential tramping gear: waterproof jacket, layers, sturdy boots, first aid kit, headlamp, and sufficient food. The track is well-marked but weather can change rapidly.

day_by_day.morning: Day 2 of the Routeburn Track. Hike from Routeburn Falls Hut over Harris Saddle (1255m) - the highest point of the track with breathtaking 360-degree views. Side trip to Conical Hill (optional, 45 minutes return) for even more spectacular panoramas
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from Harris Saddle to Lake Mackenzie Hut (approximately 4-5 hours total from Routeburn Falls). Walk along the shores of beautiful Lake Mackenzie, one of the most scenic spots on the entire track
day_by_day.evening: Relax at Lake Mackenzie Hut, dry out gear, and enjoy the serene mountain lake setting. Socialize with fellow trampers and share trail stories around the hut common room

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at Routeburn Falls Hut - oats, muesli, instant coffee
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch - energy bars, cheese, crackers, dried fruit and nuts
meals.dinner: Self-catered at Lake Mackenzie Hut - dehydrated mountain meal or pre-packed dinner. Supplement with hot chocolate and snacks

day_by_day.notes: Harris Saddle can be exposed and cold even in November - pack an extra warm layer and waterproof pants. If weather is poor, the track warden can advise on conditions. The Routeburn Track is one of New Zealand's most beautiful Great Walks - take time to soak in the views rather than rushing.

day_by_day.morning: Day 3 of the Routeburn Track. Hike from Lake Mackenzie Hut through the Orchard and Earland Falls (174m waterfall) toward Routeburn Flats Hut (approximately 4-5 hours, 13km). The track descends through ancient podocarp and beech forest
day_by_day.afternoon: Complete the final section from Routeburn Flats to Routeburn Shelter (approximately 1.5 hours, 5km) through open river flats with stunning mountain backdrops. Shuttle transfer back to Queenstown
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown Boutique Stay in Nevis Valley. Celebrate completing the Routeburn Track with a well-deserved hot shower and comfortable bed

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at Lake Mackenzie Hut before departure
meals.lunch: Final trail lunch on the track - use up remaining packed food supplies
meals.dinner: Celebrate at Queenstown's Amisfield Bistro or Botswana Butchery - treat yourself to a proper sit-down meal with Central Otago wine after three days on the trail (~NZD 55-75 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Arrange shuttle pickup from Routeburn Shelter back to Queenstown in advance. The shuttle takes approximately 1.5 hours. You will arrive back in Queenstown in the late afternoon. Book a recovery massage at one of Queenstown's day spas for the evening if budget allows.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery day in Queenstown. Sleep in and take a gentle morning walk along the Queenstown Gardens peninsula - flat, easy walking through rose gardens and sculptures with lake views
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the Skyline Gondola up Bob's Peak for panoramic views over Queenstown and Lake Wakatipu. Explore the walking tracks at the top, including the Tiki Trail descent on foot (45 minutes down through native bush)
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Queenstown waterfront and browse local shops and galleries. Watch the sunset from the lakefront before heading to dinner

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at Bespoke Kitchen - excellent healthy options, smoothies and brunch dishes (~NZD 20-28)
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at the Skyline complex at the top of the gondola, or bring a picnic to enjoy at the summit viewpoint
meals.dinner: Pier 19 on the lakefront - fresh seafood and New Zealand green-lipped mussels with views over Lake Wakatipu (~NZD 40-55 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Day 8 is intentionally relaxed to allow recovery from the three-day Routeburn Track. Listen to your body - if muscles are sore, prioritize rest and gentle movement over strenuous activities. The Queenstown Gardens walk is perfect for active recovery.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Queenstown to Wanaka (approximately 1 hour via Crown Range Road - the highest sealed road in New Zealand with spectacular views). Stop at the Crown Range summit lookout
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Roy's Peak Track from Wanaka township (16km return, 5-6 hours, 1200m elevation gain) - one of New Zealand's most photographed hikes with iconic Lake Wanaka views. Start early to avoid afternoon crowds at the famous viewpoint
day_by_day.evening: Return to Wanaka township and enjoy the charming lakeside village atmosphere. Browse the waterfront and watch the last light on the mountains

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before departing Queenstown - Vudu Larder or grab supplies from a supermarket for the trail
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on Roy's Peak - energy is essential for this demanding climb. Bring plenty of water and snacks
meals.dinner: Francesca's Italian Kitchen in Wanaka - excellent wood-fired pizza and pasta in a relaxed atmosphere (~NZD 30-45 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Roy's Peak is a challenging but non-technical hike. Start by 8:00 AM to beat the heat and crowds at the famous photo spot. The track is on private farmland - stay on the marked trail. Arrange overnight accommodation in Wanaka for this night. Drive back to Queenstown the following morning.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Wanaka before returning to Queenstown. Visit the Puzzling World attraction or take a short walk to the famous lone willow tree in Lake Wanaka - an iconic New Zealand photography spot. Walk the easy Lake Wanaka Outlet Track
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive back to Queenstown via Crown Range Road. Stop at Cardrona for a look at the historic Cardrona Hotel (1863), one of New Zealand's oldest pubs. Afternoon free in Queenstown for shopping, spa or relaxation
day_by_day.evening: Second attempt at any Queenstown experiences you may have missed, or simply enjoy the lakefront ambiance as the mountains glow in the evening light

meals.breakfast: Breakfast in Wanaka - Kika restaurant for excellent brunch options with locally sourced ingredients (~NZD 22-30)
meals.lunch: Cardrona Hotel for a classic pub lunch - pies, burgers and local ales in a historic gold rush setting (~NZD 20-30)
meals.dinner: Hawthorne Coffee House or Winnies Gourmet Pizza Bar in Queenstown - relaxed mid-range dining (~NZD 25-40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Crown Range Road can be winding - drive carefully, especially if weather is poor. The Cardrona Hotel stop adds only 10 minutes to the journey and is a quintessential New Zealand experience. Return to the Nevis Valley boutique stay by mid-afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Queenstown to Franz Josef Glacier on the West Coast (approximately 4.5-5 hours via Haast Pass). This is one of New Zealand's most spectacular drives through the Southern Alps. Stop at Haast Pass lookout and Blue Pools for a short walk
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Franz Josef township and check in to West Coast accommodation. Head immediately to the Franz Josef Glacier Valley Walk - a guided valley floor walk through ancient rainforest to the terminal face of the famous glacier
day_by_day.evening: Explore the small township of Franz Josef. Visit the local hot pools (Franz Josef Hot Pools) for a relaxing soak after the long drive - perfect for tired legs

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the Queenstown boutique stay before the long drive
meals.lunch: Stop in Haast township at the Haast River Cafe - basic but convenient, pies and sandwiches for a road trip lunch
meals.dinner: The Landing Bar and Restaurant in Franz Josef - casual dining with West Coast whitebait fritters, a local delicacy (~NZD 35-50 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Depart Queenstown by 8:00 AM for the long drive to Franz Josef. The Haast Pass route (SH6) is stunning but takes time - do not rush. Blue Pools walk is approximately 45 minutes return and well worth the stop. Fuel up in Wanaka or Haast as petrol stations are scarce on this route. Book Franz Josef accommodation in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Take a helicopter flight over the Franz Josef and Fox Glaciers with a snow landing on the neve (glacier snowfield) - a truly unforgettable West Coast experience. This is a splurge worth considering even on a mid-range budget (~NZD 280-350 per person)
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Alex Knob Track from Franz Josef township (17km return, 6-7 hours) for elevated views over the glacier and Tasman Sea, or opt for the shorter Sentinel Rock Walk and Roberts Point Track for glacier valley views without the full commitment
day_by_day.evening: Final evening on the West Coast. Enjoy the raw, wild atmosphere of Westland - watch for kea parrots near the township at dusk

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before the helicopter flight - Blue Ice Restaurant in Franz Josef for eggs and toast
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the afternoon hike, or return to township for a casual lunch at Snakebite Brewery
meals.dinner: Blue Ice Restaurant for dinner - the best dining option in Franz Josef with venison, salmon and West Coast specialties (~NZD 40-55 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter flights are weather-dependent and can be cancelled on short notice - have a backup plan. Book the helicopter in advance but confirm on the morning of the flight. The Alex Knob Track is long but offers the best elevated glacier views without requiring a guided glacier walk. Bring sun protection as UV is intense at elevation.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on the South Island. Take a peaceful walk through the Rainforest to the Glacier viewpoint one last time, or explore the Waiho River area near the glacier terminal. Pack and check out of Franz Josef accommodation
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the journey toward Christchurch or Queenstown for your onward flight (approximately 4.5 hours to Christchurch via Greymouth and Arthur's Pass, or fly from Hokitika). Alternatively, fly directly from Hokitika Airport to Christchurch (30 minutes)
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at your departure city. If time permits, enjoy a final New Zealand dinner and reflect on an extraordinary 13 days on the South Island

meals.breakfast: Final West Coast breakfast - try the whitebait fritters one more time at a local cafe in Franz Josef
meals.lunch: If driving via Arthur's Pass, stop at the Arthur's Pass Village Store and Cafe for soup and sandwiches in the alpine village
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner in Christchurch if departing from there - try Gatherings restaurant for a beautiful locally-sourced seasonal menu (~NZD 45-65 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your departure flight details and allow ample time for the drive. If flying out of Christchurch, consider an internal flight from Hokitika to Christchurch to save driving time. Return rental car with a full tank of fuel. The South Island has been extraordinary - the Routeburn Track, Nevis Bungy, Milford Sound kayaking and Franz Josef Glacier represent some of the world's finest outdoor experiences.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium New Zealand South Island Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Take the ultimate leap from New Zealand's highest bungy jump at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. This iconic AJ Hackett experience includes a scenic gondola ride to the pod suspended above the canyon and delivers an adrenaline rush unlike any other in the Southern Hemisphere.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Great Walk
experiences.description: Hike one of New Zealand's nine Great Walks through stunning alpine scenery connecting Fiordland and Mount Aspiring National Parks. The trail winds past glacial lakes, ancient beech forests, and dramatic mountain passes offering breathtaking panoramic views of the Southern Alps.

experiences.name: Franz Josef Glacier Valley Walk
experiences.description: Explore the terminal face of the famous Franz Josef Glacier on a guided valley floor walk through rainforest and glacial moraine. Witness towering ice formations and learn about the glacier's dynamic movement in one of the world's rare places where a glacier descends into a temperate rainforest.

experiences.name: Milford Sound Kayaking and Hike Combo
experiences.description: Paddle through the majestic fiords of Milford Sound surrounded by sheer 1200-meter cliff faces and cascading waterfalls, then hike a section of the Milford Track through ancient rainforest. Spot seals, dolphins, and rare Fiordland penguins in one of the world's most dramatic natural landscapes.

experiences.name: Queenstown Night Food and Culture Walk
experiences.description: Explore Queenstown's vibrant culinary scene on a guided evening walk sampling local Central Otago pinot noir, South Island lamb dishes, fresh blue cod, and artisan cheeses at iconic local eateries. Discover the town's gold rush history and Māori cultural heritage through storytelling at key landmarks along the lakefront.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Queenstown Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and prepare for transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from Queenstown Airport to Nevis Valley Boutique Stay. Settle into your suite, enjoy a welcome champagne reception and orientation with your personal concierge. Take a leisurely stroll around the boutique property grounds and soak in the dramatic Nevis Valley landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed welcome dinner at the boutique stay's private dining experience or a short drive to Queenstown for dinner at Amisfield Winery & Bistro, celebrating the start of your South Island adventure with Central Otago wines and seasonal tasting menus.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — mid-day arrival
meals.lunch: Light grazing platter and refreshments upon check-in at the boutique stay
meals.dinner: Amisfield Winery & Bistro — multi-course tasting menu paired with estate Central Otago Pinot Noir

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day — keep the schedule relaxed. Confirm all upcoming bookings with your concierge. Ensure adventure gear and hiking boots are unpacked and ready for early starts ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a premium guided sunrise hike in the Nevis Valley highlands — a private guided walk through tussock grasslands with panoramic views of the Remarkables and surrounding ranges. Your guide will share geological and Māori cultural insights along the trail.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Nevis Bungy site for the legendary Nevis Bungy Jump — New Zealand's highest bungy at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. A private pod transfer takes you to the suspended cable car platform. Experience the ultimate adrenaline rush with optional video and photography package included.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the boutique stay for a restorative spa treatment — book a 60-minute deep tissue massage or hot stone therapy to recover from the day's adventure. Enjoy a private chef dinner at the property.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay — eggs Benedict with smoked salmon, fresh fruit, artisan breads and barista coffee
meals.lunch: Packed premium picnic lunch provided at the Nevis Bungy site — antipasto, local cheeses, charcuterie and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Private chef dinner at Nevis Valley Boutique Stay — slow-roasted Central Otago lamb with seasonal vegetables and a curated wine flight

day_by_day.notes: Nevis Bungy requires comfortable clothing and closed-toe shoes. Weight limits apply (45–150kg). Book the video package in advance for a lasting memory. Weather can affect jump windows — your concierge will monitor conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Private half-day guided hike along the Ben Lomond Track above Queenstown — a challenging but rewarding alpine trail with sweeping views over Lake Wakatipu and the Remarkables. Your luxury guide service provides gourmet trail snacks and expert local commentary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend back to Queenstown and enjoy a premium wine tasting at Peregrine Wines, one of Central Otago's most architecturally stunning wineries. Enjoy a curated flight of Pinot Noir, Riesling and Pinot Gris with a sommelier-led session.
day_by_day.evening: Queenstown Night Food and Culture Walk — join a guided evening walk through Queenstown's vibrant culinary scene, sampling local Central Otago pinot noir, artisan cheeses, craft beers and gourmet street bites at curated stops across town.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay — smashed avocado, poached eggs, sourdough and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Grazing platter and wine pairings at Peregrine Wines cellar door
meals.dinner: Included tastings on the Night Food and Culture Walk — supplement with a nightcap at Queenstown's Rata restaurant bar

day_by_day.notes: Ben Lomond hike is approximately 4–5 hours return. Wear layered clothing as alpine conditions can change rapidly. The Night Food Walk typically departs around 6:00–6:30pm — confirm exact timing with your concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Luxury scenic helicopter flight from Queenstown over Fiordland National Park, landing on a remote alpine peak for a private guided walk with breathtaking views — a bucket-list experience exclusive to premium travelers. Champagne toast on the summit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Fly or drive to Te Anau (approximately 2.5 hours by private vehicle from Queenstown). Check in at a premium Te Anau lodge such as Fiordland Lodge. Afternoon at leisure to explore the shores of Lake Te Anau or take a short guided walk in the beech forest.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at the Fiordland Lodge dining room overlooking Lake Te Anau — a refined menu featuring South Island venison, Fiordland crayfish and local produce, paired with Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at Nevis Valley Boutique Stay before departure
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed lunch enjoyed during the helicopter alpine experience or at a scenic lakeside stop en route to Te Anau
meals.dinner: Fiordland Lodge restaurant — three-course dinner with lake views and curated New Zealand wine list

day_by_day.notes: This is a transition day from Nevis Valley/Queenstown to Te Anau in preparation for the Milford Sound and Routeburn experiences. Confirm helicopter booking 48 hours in advance. Private vehicle transfer to Te Anau is recommended for luggage flexibility.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Te Anau early for the iconic Milford Sound Kayaking and Hike Combo — paddle through the majestic fiords of Milford Sound surrounded by sheer 1,200-meter cliff faces, cascading waterfalls and resident pods of dolphins and fur seals. A premium guided experience with expert naturalist commentary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Milford Sound combo with a guided hike along the Milford foreshore and rainforest trails, exploring the lush Fiordland vegetation. Alternatively, upgrade to a private Milford Sound small-group boat cruise for an intimate fiord experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Te Anau by private transfer. Enjoy a relaxing evening at Fiordland Lodge — optional twilight walk along the lake edge before a gourmet dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early continental breakfast at Fiordland Lodge before departure
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed lunch provided as part of the Milford kayaking experience — enjoyed on the fiord shore
meals.dinner: Fiordland Lodge — chef's seasonal tasting menu with Fiordland crayfish bisque, South Island lamb and a Central Otago Pinot Noir pairing

day_by_day.notes: Milford Sound road (SH94) is spectacular — allow 2.5 hours each way from Te Anau. Kayaking requires moderate fitness. Waterproof layers are essential as Milford Sound averages over 7 meters of rain annually. November is a beautiful time with waterfalls at full flow.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the Routeburn Track Great Walk — one of New Zealand's finest alpine trails connecting Fiordland and Mount Aspiring National Parks. Day 1 of a premium guided multi-day walk: start at the Routeburn Shelter near Glenorchy, hiking through ancient beech forests to the Routeburn Flats. Your luxury guided walk includes a private guide, premium gear and gourmet trail provisions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the track to Routeburn Falls Hut area — enjoy dramatic views of the cascading Routeburn Falls and expansive alpine meadows. The afternoon section offers spectacular scenery with minimal crowds on this premium guided experience.
day_by_day.evening: Overnight at a premium private hut or lodge accommodation on the Routeburn Track (private hut booking for exclusive use). Enjoy a hot cooked dinner prepared by your guide, fine wine and stargazing in one of New Zealand's darkest sky regions.

meals.breakfast: Hearty hot breakfast at Fiordland Lodge before departure to the trailhead
meals.lunch: Gourmet trail lunch at Routeburn Flats — artisan sandwiches, energy bars, fresh fruit and thermos coffee
meals.dinner: Guide-prepared hot dinner at the private hut — hearty backcountry gourmet meal with New Zealand wine

day_by_day.notes: The Routeburn Track is a multi-day experience. Pack light — your guide service will arrange a porter for heavier luggage if needed. Layered merino wool clothing is recommended. November weather can be variable — waterproof jacket is essential. Confirm hut booking exclusivity with your luxury guiding company.

day_by_day.morning: Routeburn Track Day 2 — hike from Routeburn Falls up to the spectacular Harris Saddle (1,255m), the high point of the track. On a clear November day, the panoramic views across Fiordland and the Darran Mountains are extraordinary. Your guide will identify key peaks and share alpine ecology insights.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from Harris Saddle toward Lake Mackenzie — a stunning turquoise alpine lake set beneath towering peaks. Arrive at Lake Mackenzie Hut area for a well-earned rest. Optional short side trip to the Earland Falls viewpoint.
day_by_day.evening: Second night on the Routeburn Track at Lake Mackenzie private hut accommodation. Celebrate the halfway point with a special guide-prepared dinner and a premium bottle of Central Otago Pinot Noir brought in by your support team.

meals.breakfast: Hot porridge, eggs and coffee at the private hut — fuel for the big alpine day ahead
meals.lunch: Packed premium trail lunch at Harris Saddle — enjoyed with 360-degree mountain views
meals.dinner: Guide-prepared gourmet dinner at Lake Mackenzie hut — New Zealand beef stew, crusty bread and wine

day_by_day.notes: Harris Saddle can be exposed and windy — extra warm layers and gloves are recommended even in November. The Lake Mackenzie section is among the most photographed on the track. Ensure camera batteries are fully charged.

day_by_day.morning: Routeburn Track Day 3 — final section from Lake Mackenzie through the Hollyford Valley and ancient podocarp forest to the Divide (the western end of the track). This section showcases the lush Fiordland rainforest and the dramatic contrast between alpine and lowland ecosystems.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private vehicle transfer from the Divide back to Queenstown via the scenic Hollyford Valley and Te Anau. Stop at a scenic viewpoint for a celebratory champagne toast marking the completion of the Routeburn Great Walk. Return to Nevis Valley Boutique Stay.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxation evening at the boutique stay — enjoy a private spa session, hot tub under the stars and a celebratory dinner prepared by the property's private chef.

meals.breakfast: Hot breakfast at Lake Mackenzie hut before the final day's hiking
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed trail lunch on the final Routeburn section
meals.dinner: Private chef dinner at Nevis Valley Boutique Stay — celebration menu featuring Central Otago duck confit, truffle risotto and a premium wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Transfer from the Divide to Queenstown takes approximately 2.5–3 hours. Your concierge should arrange the private vehicle pickup in advance. This is a well-earned rest evening — take full advantage of the boutique stay's spa and wellness facilities.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning at the Nevis Valley Boutique Stay. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely gourmet breakfast and take a gentle walk around the property grounds. Optional in-room yoga or stretching session to ease post-trek muscles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided e-bike tour through the Gibbston Valley wine region — explore the 'Valley of the Vines' on electric bikes, stopping at premium cellar doors including Peregrine, Gibbston Valley Winery and Brennan Wines for tastings. A relaxed but indulgent afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Rata Restaurant in Queenstown — one of the South Island's finest dining establishments, helmed by renowned chef Josh Emmett. Expect elevated New Zealand cuisine in a sophisticated atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Extended leisurely breakfast at the boutique stay — full hot breakfast with pastries, fresh juices and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Wine and cheese pairings at Gibbston Valley Winery cellar door — artisan cheese board with estate wines
meals.dinner: Rata Restaurant, Queenstown — à la carte dinner with New Zealand lamb, sustainable seafood and a sommelier-curated wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Day 9 is intentionally slower-paced after three days on the Routeburn Track. The e-bike tour is suitable for all fitness levels and can be arranged through your concierge. Rata Restaurant requires advance booking — reserve at least 2 weeks ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury drive to the West Coast — depart Queenstown via the Haast Pass (SH6), one of New Zealand's most scenic mountain highways. Stop at Thunder Creek Falls and the Gates of Haast for short walks and photography. Travel time approximately 3.5–4 hours to Franz Josef.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in at a premium Franz Josef property such as The Terrace Motel or a luxury boutique lodge. After settling in, join the Franz Josef Glacier Valley Walk — a guided walk to the terminal face of the famous Franz Josef Glacier through lush rainforest and dramatic glacial outwash plains, with expert glaciological commentary.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Franz Josef village at a top local restaurant — The Landing Bar & Restaurant offers quality West Coast cuisine featuring whitebait fritters, venison and local craft beer.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at Nevis Valley Boutique Stay before the long drive
meals.lunch: Scenic roadside picnic lunch at a stunning Haast Pass viewpoint — premium provisions prepared by the boutique stay
meals.dinner: The Landing Bar & Restaurant, Franz Josef — West Coast whitebait fritters, pan-seared venison and Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc

day_by_day.notes: The Haast Pass drive is long but extraordinarily scenic — allow extra time for stops. The Franz Josef Glacier has retreated significantly in recent years; the valley walk is still a powerful and educational experience. Sandflies are active on the West Coast — bring strong insect repellent.

day_by_day.morning: Premium heli-hike on Franz Josef Glacier — a luxury helicopter flight to the upper glacier ice fields, landing on the ancient blue ice for a guided walk with crampons through seracs, crevasses and ice caves. One of New Zealand's most exclusive adventure experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Franz Josef village and enjoy a relaxing afternoon at a local hot pools facility (Waiho Hot Pools) — soak in geothermal pools surrounded by rainforest. Optional rainforest guided walk through the Tatare Tunnels or Peters Pool track.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell West Coast dinner — enjoy a curated tasting menu at your lodge or a premium dining experience in Franz Josef. Reflect on the glacier experience over a glass of Central Otago Pinot Noir.

meals.breakfast: Early gourmet breakfast at the lodge before the helicopter departure
meals.lunch: Light post-heli-hike lunch at the lodge — fresh sandwiches, fruit and hot soup
meals.dinner: Premium lodge dinner or The Landing — chef's special featuring West Coast crayfish, local lamb and a New Zealand cheese board to finish

day_by_day.notes: Heli-hike operations are weather-dependent — Franz Josef weather changes rapidly. Have a flexible backup plan such as a guided rainforest walk. Book the heli-hike as early as possible and reconfirm the morning of. Crampons and ice axes are provided by the operator.

day_by_day.morning: Scenic drive from Franz Josef back toward Queenstown via the West Coast and Wanaka — stop at the famous Lake Matheson Mirror Lake for a morning reflection walk (best light is early morning) capturing the iconic reflections of Aoraki/Mount Cook and Mount Tasman.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Wanaka — arrive for lunch and spend the afternoon exploring this charming lakeside town. Visit Rippon Vineyard, one of New Zealand's most beautifully situated wineries on the shores of Lake Wanaka, for a premium tasting experience. Optional stand-up paddleboarding on Lake Wanaka.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Wanaka at Francesca's Italian Kitchen or Ritual Café — enjoy a relaxed, high-quality dinner before the final drive back to Queenstown and the Nevis Valley Boutique Stay.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the Franz Josef lodge to maximize morning light at Lake Matheson
meals.lunch: Wanaka lakefront lunch at Kika restaurant — modern New Zealand cuisine with local ingredients and lake views
meals.dinner: Francesca's Italian Kitchen, Wanaka — wood-fired pizza, handmade pasta and Italian wines in a warm, intimate setting

day_by_day.notes: Lake Matheson is best visited at sunrise or early morning for the clearest reflections — plan your departure from Franz Josef accordingly. The drive from Wanaka to Queenstown is approximately 1 hour via the Crown Range Road — a spectacular alpine route. Return to Nevis Valley Boutique Stay for the final night.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at the Nevis Valley Boutique Stay — enjoy a slow, indulgent farewell breakfast. Take a final walk on the property grounds, capturing last views of the Nevis Valley landscape. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to Queenstown Airport. If time allows before departure, stop at Queenstown's Steamer Wharf for a final coffee and lake views, or browse premium New Zealand souvenirs and artisan goods at local boutiques along the waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Queenstown — farewell to the South Island. Departure flight arrangements as per your booking.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the boutique stay — the full works, including eggs your way, smoked salmon, fresh pastries, fruit platters and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch or coffee at Queenstown waterfront before airport transfer — Joe's Garage or Vudu Café & Larder for quality café fare
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2 hours before departure for Queenstown Airport check-in. Pick up any last New Zealand Merino wool gifts, Manuka honey or Central Otago wines at the airport duty-free. Ensure all adventure photos and videos from the Nevis Bungy and heli-hike are downloaded and backed up before departure.
